page: Microsoft Azure F2als_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine belonging to the Falsv7 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, operating at a high base clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache per core. It is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is capable of mounting Premium Storage.

In benchmark testing, the F2als_v7 demonstrates strong single-core performance. Stress-ng single-core CPU testing and single-threaded gzip compression both rank in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also achieves top-tier performance. However, multi-threaded operations and memory-bound tasks show some limitations. Multi-core stress-ng performance and Passmark CPU scores fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark memory scores are positioned in the weak tier (bottom 25%). Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only large block speeds at 51.88 GB/sec and write speeds at 34.76 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F2als_v7 offers a high-frequency compute profile for workloads that do not require large memory footprints or local storage. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores provide predictable execution without the CPU credit limitations of burstable instances. This makes the server suitable for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, and basic computational workloads. However, the 4.0 GB memory constraint and weak multi-threaded decompression performance make it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or heavy parallel processing.
